detail.longDescription: After reading this Q&A , I decided to try using Ellipsis as a function argument default: def func(arg: int = ...): print(arg) However, Pyright complains: Expression of type "EllipsisType" cannot be assigned to parameter of type "int" "EllipsisType" is not assignable to "int" Because ... isn't an int . So I tried using a Union : def func(arg: int | Ellipsis = ...): print(arg) Pyright still complains: Variable not allowed in type expression (variable) Ellipsis: Unknown It only works if the function body is a literal Ellipsis (not print(arg) or even pass ): def func(arg: int = ...): # happy pyright! ... Why does it work here but not anywhere else? How can I make ... work in all situations?
